workingTitle: Helium reveals a double detonation in supernova 2024kce
coreFacts: SN 2024kce was discovered in M49 on June 2, 2024 and classified as a peculiar Type Ia supernova three days later.
Simultaneous optical and near-infrared spectra obtained eleven days before maximum light showed helium absorption at 1.083 micrometres, 2.058 micrometres, and 7065 angstroms.
All three helium signatures are consistent with ejecta moving at 16,400 kilometres per second, above the 12,500 kilometres per second photosphere.
The authors report this as the first helium detection before maximum light in a thermonuclear supernova.
A double-detonation calculation with a 0.69-solar-mass carbon-oxygen white dwarf and 0.09-solar-mass helium shell reproduced several observed features, including the high-velocity helium absorption.
The supernova combines traits of subluminous Type Ia events and calcium-rich transients.
caveats: The study is an unreviewed preprint, so its interpretation remains preliminary.
The 1.024-micrometre trough is blended: the paper finds helium is present, but carbon and magnesium can also contribute to this wavelength region.
The double-detonation origin is inferred from the helium location, its excitation requirements, and agreement with one detailed model; the explosion mechanism was not observed directly.
The preferred model does not reproduce every spectral feature and diverges from the later near-infrared data as simplifying assumptions become less adequate.
One unusual event cannot establish that all calcium-rich or faint Type Ia supernovae share this origin.
